pairs.evidence: crates/core/tests/datasets_batch_equivalence.rs:139 The differential batch-vs-per-record test reports 'no divergence' per round but never asserts that the removed/changed paths actually fired in any round, so a no-difference verdict over a population the mechanism never reached is indistinguishable from real equivalence.

techniques.evidence: crates/core/tests/datasets_batch_equivalence.rs:139 Only equality between the two paths is asserted; there is no engagement count (e.g. removed>0 somewhere) beside the verdict.

crates/core/tests/datasets.rs:15 Every test builds a fresh SQLite store and runs the full 56-migration chain (Storage::connect); no build-once template copied per test. The reaper is named (TempStore Drop).
crates/core/tests/datasets_bulk_perf.rs:127 Cost harnesses are scheduled lanes that emit artifacts; pre-declared criteria are judged by an external certifier, not asserted in the test.

crates/core/tests/derived_backfill_perf.rs:16 Here the claim is cost (duration), which the technique excludes; the harness already uses a host-independent ratio, and no concurrency is asserted by stopwatch.
crates/core/tests/fingerprint_shared_dom.rs:50 The corpus is derived from read_dir and carries a floor, so an emptied selection fails instead of passing green.

pairs.subject: test-harness
pairs.evidence: crates/server/src/routes/meta.rs:1281 The /metrics exposition is text for a foreign reader (a Prometheus scraper), but it is asserted with a home-grown whitespace lint rather than by running a real exposition parser (no Prometheus parser crate exists in the repo), so a body the reader rejects or misreads can pass.

techniques.evidence: crates/server/src/routes/meta.rs:1281 A near-side model of the reader stands in for the reader; it targets one known defect shape, not parse validity.
crates/server/src/routes/meta.rs:1285 The test seeds the exact defect, shows that contains() is blind to it, and asserts the checker reports every shape.
crates/server/src/routes/meta.rs:1319 The source guard excludes test modules by span (not by truncation), drops comment lines, uses str::lines (CRLF-safe), and keeps its reason in the asserting file.
crates/server/src/routes/meta.rs:1345 The derived production-line population declares a floor, so an empty walk cannot pass.
crates/server/src/routes/meta.rs:73 Where a cache or a re-render could produce the same bytes, the test asserts the producer (pointer identity) and separately asserts equality with a fresh render.
crates/server/src/routes/meta.rs:98 The render-cost timing is printed, not asserted, so there is no stopwatch verdict.

pairs.registryProposal: assert-through-the-reader frames the reader as a locally installed tool (shell, VCS, package manager); it could say explicitly that when the reader is a remote consumer (a metrics scraper, an API client), the reader's own published parser library is the unit-cost oracle, and that a hand-written lint of known defect shapes is the near-side assertion the technique warns against.
